title: Average Acceleration and Instantaneous Acceleration
theory:
**Big idea:** Acceleration is the rate of change of **velocity**. Since velocity is a vector, changing the speed, the direction, or both means the body is accelerating.

- **Uniform velocity:** the velocity stays the same (same speed and same direction), so there is no acceleration.
- **Accelerated motion:** the velocity changes in magnitude, direction or both.

**Average acceleration**
**a_av = (v₂ – v₁) / (t₂ – t₁)**
It depends only on the velocities at t₁ and t₂, not on how the velocity changed in between.

**Instantaneous acceleration** (just called "acceleration")
**a = lim (Δt → 0) Δv/Δt = dv/dt**

**Units:** m/s². Dimensions: **LT⁻²**.

**🧮 Worked example: turning without speeding up**
A car's velocity changes from 10 m/s east to 10 m/s north in 2 s.
Δ**v** = **v₂** – **v₁** has magnitude √(10² + 10²) = 10√2 m/s.
a_av = 10√2 / 2 = **5√2 ≈ 7.1 m/s²**, even though the speed never changed!

**🧮 Worked example:** v = 3t² + 2 (m/s). Then a = dv/dt = 6t. At t = 2 s, **a = 12 m/s²**.

> ⚠️ **Common misconception:** "Constant speed means no acceleration." A car going round a bend at a steady speed **is** accelerating, because its direction changes.

questions.prompt: The SI unit of acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Acceleration is velocity (m/s) per second, so m/s².

questions.prompt: A car goes round a circular track at a constant speed. The car is:

options.text: Not accelerating, because its speed is constant
Accelerating, because the direction of its velocity keeps changing

questions.explanation: A change in direction is a change in velocity, so the car is accelerating.

questions.prompt: The velocity of a body changes from 10 m/s towards east to 10 m/s towards north in 2 s. The magnitude of its average acceleration is:
questions.explanation: The change in velocity has magnitude 10√2 m/s. Divided by 2 s, that is 5√2 m/s² ≈ 7.1 m/s².

questions.prompt: The dimensional formula of acceleration is:
The velocity of a particle is v = 3t² + 2 (in m/s, t in s). Its acceleration at t = 2 s is:
questions.explanation: a = dv/dt = 6t = 12 m/s². (14 is the velocity at t = 2 s.)
